newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far-right for boycott of foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Austria far-right for boycott of foreign workers.

text.p: A regional branch of Austria's far-right Freedom Party caused political uproar on Thursday when it directed public building contracts should only go to firms that did not employ foreign workers.
Karl-Heinz Grasser, the Freedom Party's economic spokesman in the southern province of Carinthia, said the move was in response to unemployment in the region of around 30,000.
"Our priority should be to ensure that Carinthian men and women have jobs," Grasser said in a statement.
Unions and employers hit out at the directive, however, while lawyers doubted its legality. Some political opponents demanded Grasser's resignation.
"This directive has no legal basis and it is against every guideline on awarding public orders," said the Chamber of Economy, which represents employers.
Workers from Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia are thought to account for 15 to 20 percent of the construction workforce in Carinthia.
"The Carinthia Freedom Party has gone one step further towards a thoroughly inhuman policy towards foreigners," said regional Social Democrat politician Robert Elmecker.
Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider was forced to resign as governor of Carinthia in 1991 after he praised Adolf Hitler's labour policies.

In European parliamentary elections last October Haider's Freedom Party won the biggest number of votes in Carinthia. Nationally it is the third strongest party and Europe's biggest far-right parliamentary grouping.
